solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Priest avoids dangerous situation, producing sacred text

indicators.note: the priest keeps away from the trap, so his letter is dropped from it

parts.note: a mantrap is a trap for people, hence any dangerous situation

explanation.surface: A cleric steers clear of trouble and comes up with a holy writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu or Buddhist chant or verse used in prayer and meditation counts as a sacred text.

clue.text: Wear down nail breaking into casualty department

indicators.note: the nail forces its way inside the hospital department

parts.note: A and E (accident and emergency) is the British hospital casualty department
a brad is a thin flat nail

explanation.surface: A worn-down nail being smashed into the emergency ward.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrape or rub something away by friction is to erode or wear it down.

clue.text: A bracelet is whipped? That can be tracked down

indicators.note: something whipped is stirred up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A stolen bracelet, which police can follow up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be followed and found again is able to be traced.

clue.text: Director tucked into beer and hot food around Suffolk town

indicators.note: the director is placed inside the beer

parts.note: ale is beer

indicators.note: the slang word for food is turned around

parts.note: grub is slang for food
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A film director tucks into beer and hot food somewhere in Suffolk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the slang word for food backwards. Suffolk is a county in eastern England; this is a seaside town there.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldeburgh is a coastal town in Suffolk, home of the Britten music festival.

clue.text: Standing back, one's caught in draught

indicators.note: the reversed piece is held within the draught, as if trapped inside it

parts.note: a draught is a dose of drink or medicine, a potion

indicators.note: back says the letters for one's run in the other direction

parts.note: one's is I'S, one (I) plus the 's

explanation.surface: Someone standing at the back is caught in a cold current of air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing' looks like part of the picture of someone at the back, but it is the definition, in the sense of rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's standing in society is their rank or status, their place in the order of things.

clue.text: A noble without equal's all but 50

indicators.note: everything except the 50 is kept

parts.note: something without equal is peerless; the 's is no letter
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: A unique aristocrat is almost fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman holding a title in the peerage, such as a duchess or baroness, is a noble.

clue.text: Some surprise guests follow without pause

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few unexpected visitors trail straight in.
explanation.definitionFit: In music or broadcasting, to move straight on from one item to the next is to segue.

clue.text: Auditor's dogged, producing a booklet

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the word is as heard

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow, so dogged means tracked

explanation.surface: An accountant was hounded into publishing a small pamphlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' looks like an accountant but is just a listener.
explanation.definitionFit: A short pamphlet, often religious or political, is a tract.

clue.text: First off, cunning idiot could be one of these

definitions.text: First off, cunning idiot could be one of these

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for cunning is taken away

parts.note: foxy means cunning
a moron is an idiot

explanation.surface: The phrase 'cunning idiot' itself is an example of a contradiction in terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure of speech joining contradictory terms, such as a clever fool, fits the whole clue.

clue.text: Stop working on newspaper? That's material

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: a newspaper is an organ, a publication speaking for a group
a machine that stops working is said to die

explanation.surface: A question about downing tools on a newspaper, apparently a material issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Organdie is a fine stiff cotton fabric, a kind of material.

clue.text: Gwent (for a start) woman's name?

indicators.note: only the opening letter of Gwent is wanted, its start

parts.note: woman's gives LADY'S, a lady being a woman

explanation.surface: Asks whether a certain Welsh county name is a woman's name.
explanation.walkthrough: Gwent is a historic county in south Wales, and the answer is a name with Welsh roots (Gwladys).
explanation.definitionFit: Gladys is a traditional female first name, of Welsh origin.

clue.text: Braved storms heroically perhaps

indicators.note: the word braved is battered about as if by storms, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone bravely weathered storms in a heroic manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heroically' looks like part of the story of the storm, but it is an example of the part of speech defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroically is a word modifying a verb, so it is an instance of this part of speech; perhaps marks the example.

clue.text: Putting up with Left instead of Right is the people's choice

indicators.note: one letter takes the place of the other in the word for putting up

parts.note: putting up a building is its erection

explanation.surface: Tolerating a left-winger in place of a right-winger is what voters chose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting up with' reads as tolerating, but 'with' is a link and 'Putting up' is the building sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A vote is how the people pick their representatives, so it is literally their choice.

clue.text: Fish bones will be served up

indicators.note: in a down answer, served up means the letters rise, reading bottom to top

parts.note: bones is slang for a doctor, DOC

explanation.surface: Fish bones are going to be dished up.
explanation.definitionFit: The cod is a common North Atlantic food fish.

clue.text: Work of Mussorgsky and Borodin's nearly all in vogue, for a change

indicators.note: the letters are made to change their order

parts.note: Borodin's gives the letters of the composer's name and the s

indicators.note: nearly all of vogue loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Talk of Russian composers: one's work and Borodin's mostly fashionable, for once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly all' trims vogue to VOGU; with BORODINS that is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Mussorgsky's famous opera about the Russian tsar, so it is one of his works.

clue.text: Tenor appears in grand opera, in fantastic Butterfly

indicators.note: fantastic suggests a fanciful rearrangement of the letters

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A tenor sings in a grand opera, a fantastic Madama Butterfly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butterfly' calls Puccini's opera to mind; it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange-tip is a European butterfly whose males have orange wing tips.

clue.text: Inferior, not good, pill for stress

indicators.note: not good means the letter for good is removed

parts.note: an inferior is an underling, a subordinate
E is slang for an ecstasy pill

explanation.surface: A poor-quality pill to cope with stress.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise a point is to stress it, as if marking a line beneath it.

clue.text: Fight in ring

definitions.meaning: a noisy heated argument or brawl

explanation.surface: A boxing bout in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The term means a fierce exchange or a bell's chiming, two separate senses.

clue.text: Writer's drawn one up in advance

indicators.note: the rider piece goes ahead of the other in the answer

parts.note: one up on a horse is a rider
a drawn face is haggard, gaunt and tired

explanation.surface: An author has sketched someone being promoted ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: H. Rider Haggard was the Victorian novelist who wrote King Solomon's Mines, so he is a writer.

clue.text: Arnold regularly gets stick

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter of Arnold is taken

explanation.surface: A man named Arnold is regularly beaten or criticised.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod is a thin straight stick or pole.

clue.text: After illness recedes, throws out rubbish

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first
the bug goes backwards, so its letters reverse

parts.note: a bug is an illness
to bin something is to throw it out

explanation.surface: Once the sickness passes, someone clears out the junk.
explanation.definitionFit: Gubbins is British slang for odds and ends or worthless stuff, so rubbish.

clue.text: Act as inspiration for puzzle

parts.note: to be something is to act as it
a muse is a source of inspiration

explanation.surface: Serving as someone's inspiration in order to puzzle them.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewilder or confuse someone is to puzzle them.

clue.text: One has decent employment? That's just as well

parts.note: one is A, the indefinite article
decent means good
employment is a job

explanation.surface: Someone has a respectable post, which is a relief.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'it's a ... thing' expresses relief, meaning fortunate or just as well.

clue.text: Asian or European country without borders

indicators.note: the country loses its outer letters, its borders

parts.note: Romania is a country in Europe

explanation.surface: Choosing between an Asian or a European state with open frontiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Oman, on the Arabian Peninsula, is an Asian.

clue.text: Justice for one radio presenter pulled up outside university

indicators.note: the reversed letters go round the university letter
in a down answer, pulled up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: for one means for example, EG
a DJ is a disc jockey presenting radio shows

explanation.surface: A judge, say, hauls up a radio host outside a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Justice for one' looks like the definition; 'for one' is EG. 'pulled up' turns EGDJ into JDGE, which sits outside U.
explanation.definitionFit: A justice is a judicial officer in the courts, a holder of that bench role.

clue.text: A way to get inside information showing where stocks may grow

indicators.note: the first pieces are placed within the word for information

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Insider trading advice: a route to secret data showing where shares might rise.
explanation.walkthrough: Stocks are not shares here but the scented flowering plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocks are flowering plants, so a cultivated plot of ground is where they are grown.

clue.text: Party given by Jack Dee, we hear, for senile fellow

parts.note: a do is a party
a jack, or tar, is a sailor

indicators.note: the word Dee is taken as said aloud, giving a single letter

parts.note: Dee spoken is the name of the letter D

explanation.surface: A celebration thrown by comedian Jack Dee for an old man past it.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Dee is a British comedian; the name splits into jack, a sailor, and Dee, the letter's spoken name.
explanation.definitionFit: A doddering old man whose mind is failing with age is called by this slightly old-fashioned term.

clue.text: A plot to arouse your curiosity

definitions.meaning: to fascinate or make someone curious

explanation.surface: A story line designed to make you curious.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means a secret scheme; the verb means to fascinate, both senses of one word.

clue.text: Cape fruit previously creating a nasty scene?

indicators.note: the fruit comes earlier in the answer than the cape

parts.note: the ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit
a ness is a headland or cape

explanation.surface: A South African fruit has apparently caused an unpleasant incident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cape fruit' suggests something from the Cape of Good Hope, but Cape is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsightliness is the quality of a scene that is nasty to look at; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Was a hunter requested urgently? Sounds like it

indicators.note: the word for requested urgently is matched by the way it is spoken

parts.note: to pray is to ask earnestly, so prayed means requested urgently

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone hunting was summoned in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal that hunted others fed on them, which is the verb's sense of stalking victims.
